head: pr17457-r12
report:
NO DEFECTS

I found no defect I could prove at this head in the 20-minute window. I read the hold mechanism and job-manager changes in full and checked the provider transports from the earlier reports, but did not read all 17.5k lines of the diff. I did not re-run any of the earlier reviewers' probes or the checker attack scripts, so the earlier findings marked closed below are closed on source reading plus the head's own tests, not on a replay.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Status of each earlier finding at this head**

- **Claude F1 — a request waiting in the provider's retry backoff is sent after the hold engages: closed in the source.** `runInRequestHoldScope` (`packages/ai/src/request-hold.ts`) now wraps `globalThis.fetch` for the whole process. Every fetch made in a held scope waits there and is refused; it never reaches the real fetch. The Anthropic client looks up its fetch per attempt (`opts.fetch ?? fetch`, `anthropic-client.ts:260`). Its `cchFetch`/`baseFetch` (`anthropic.ts:3916`) is built on each call, not cached, so it is built after the wrapper is installed. Each retry therefore goes through the wrapper.
- **Claude F2 / Astra "raw and OAuth adapters" (Perplexity, Hindsight, MCP over HTTP, Exa, `withOAuthAccess`): closed in the source.**
  - The fetch wrapper covers raw adapters. MCP's `#fetch` (`mcp/transports/http.ts`) and the Hindsight client call the global `fetch` at call time and run in the caller's async context.
  - `withOAuthAccess` now checks the hold before every attempt (`runOAuthAttempt`), with no await between the check and the send.
  - The checker now finds the `stream<Provider>` entry points itself instead of using a fixed list (helper doc lines 10–12).
- **Astra P1 — microtask gap between admission and send: closed.** `withAuth` now runs `if (isRequestHeld()) await admitProviderRequest(...)` right before `attempt` is called. The fetch wrapper also checks in the same call as the send.
- **Astra P1 — a job that starts its owner's disposal before inserting itself misses the hold: closed.** `register` now adds the job to `#jobs` and calls `#stopForDisposingOwner` before the body runs (`job-manager.ts:469-477`).
- **Astra P2 — nested holds keep a waiting request after the owner ends: closed.** `refuseHeld` now listens to the `ended` signal of every scope in the parent chain, plus the request's own signal.
- **Claude "late survivor stays held for ever": closed.** When a binding whose disposal already fired is replaced or unbound, `bindOwnerDisposal` cancels that owner's held jobs.
- **Astra P1 — `/security cloud` sends after disposal, and live-call startup sends after the controller stops: closed per this head's tests.** `test/security/cloud-command-disposal.test.ts` and `test/live/controller-disposal.test.ts` were added, and both pass.
- **Claude F3/F4 and Astra P2 — checker bypass forms: likely closed, not attack-tested.** The checker's header now says it handles:
  - `globalThis["fetch"]` and fetch destructured from the global object;
  - computed Hindsight `client[…]` and computed dynamic imports;
  - a later spread that sets the signal (it wins);
  - every branch of a conditional;
  - helper-built options (accepted only when the signal is visible in the helper's arguments).

  I read the code that matches these forms (`globalAliasesIn`, `computedImport`, the spread handling in `supply`), but did not rerun the earlier attack scripts against it.
- **Claude F5 — a tool call already in flight is not held: closed.** At this head the tool's own fetches run inside the job's hold scope and go through the wrapper.

**Suspicions I checked and ruled out**

- **Fetch saved before the wrapper was installed:** every production `globalThis.fetch` default (aws-credentials, google-auth, google-shared, blob-broker files, exposure) is evaluated when the function runs, not when the module loads.
- **`holdAfterKeyResolution` dropping resolver metadata:** `isApiKeyResolver` is only `typeof key === "function"`, so the wrapper keeps everything that matters.
- **`withRequestHold` using `outer.fail(error)`:** this matches the error handling already used in `stream.ts` (lines 721, 830, 1358).
- **`fetch-retry` spreading `init` to add the signal:** this does not change behaviour for callers that already passed one.

**Unproven, not asserted:** `ModelRegistry.#discoverProviderModelsCoalesced` (`config/model-registry.ts:2020-2040`) shares an in-flight discovery promise across callers but is not started with `runOutsideRequestHold`, unlike its siblings in `catalog/openai-compat.ts`. If a held subagent started it, other callers would wait until that job is cancelled and then get its refusal. I found no path that shows a held job triggering a configured-provider discovery, so I am not reporting it as a defect.

**Tests run at this head**

- `packages/ai`: `request-hold.test.ts` and `request-hold-shared-work.test.ts` — 37 pass, 0 fail.
- `packages/coding-agent`: `security/cloud-command-disposal.test.ts`, `live/controller-disposal.test.ts` and `async-job-manager.test.ts` — 63 pass, 0 fail.
